newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor's Hamel sees strength despite jobs data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor's Hamel sees strength despite jobs data.

text.p: Bureau of Labor Statistics economist Harvey Hamel on Thursday said he saw strength in the U.S. job market, particularly manufacturing, despite June's rise in the unemployment rate.
"There's a lot of strength in the economy," he told Reuters Financial Television in an interview.

The unemployment rate jumped to 5.0 percent last month from a 24-year low of 4.8 percent in May as private sector job growth slowed, particularly in several service industries, the government said Thursday.
Hamel said industrial machinery, electronic components and aircrafts have continued to gain jobs. The manufacturing sector added 14,000 jobs in June, up from 5,000 in May.
"I see manufacturing employment as kind of resuming the pace ... we saw earlier this year," he said.

Hamel said wet weather contributed to the 2,000 decline in construction payrolls in June. "You have to blame the weather a bit," he said. Local government payrolls rose by 78,000 in June after a 6,000 drop in May.
"I would dismiss the increase in local government education as somewhat of a seasonal phenomenon," he said.
